content:
Army Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom accused military brass of a “tactical failure” in not protecting a logistics command post from an Iranian drone strike that killed the first six Americans in the ongoing war.

“The protection that was there was to stop car bombs and threats like that,” he told “60 Minutes” on Sunday. “There was nothing there designed to protect from an aerial attack.”

Ramsbottom’s claim on national TV rebutted Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s insistence that the Army Reserve’s 103rd Sustainment Command center at Port Shuaiba in Kuwait ― just 65 miles from Iran ― was “fortified” but got victimized by a “once in a while” “squirter.”

Before the episode ran, Ramsbottom filed a whistleblower report to the House and Senate armed services committees, alleging that concerns about drones fell on deaf ears at the Pentagon, CNN reported.

Hegseth withstood a House effort last week to launch impeachment proceedings related to the war, but Democrats likely aren’t finished with their investigations into the conflict of choice started by President Donald Trump, Hegseth and Israel.

Ramsbottom said fears of drone vulnerability were forwarded to the unit commander and Maj. Gen. John Hinson. Ramsbottom said he wasn’t satisfied with the response.

“I brought it up twice in various meetings, basically saying, ‘Hey, I don’t see how we’re protected here,’” Ramsbottom told Norah O’Donnell in the segment. “He said, ‘We don’t have to worry about protection.’”

Ramsbottom, who was injured in the attack along with dozens of others, gave a scathing assessment of a base he said has been described as a “trailer park.”

“I feel this is a tactical failure by the Army, our leadership, and myself, all the way down to my level,” he said. “Yes, we did not plan this well. And this needs to be a lesson that we learn.”

More than 800 Americans have been wounded and 23 have reportedly died in the war, which also has led to spikes in prices stateside and cost Trump and his party dearly in the midterm elections.
